hypotheses.text: Complete penetrance of neurodevelopmental impairment is restricted to KDM2B CxxC zinc finger domain variants, whereas non-CxxC loss-of-function (pLOF) and JmjC domain variants exhibit non-penetrant carriers and variable expressivity.
hypotheses.rationale: Testing this hypothesis will resolve whether neurodevelopmental impairment/intellectual disability is truly an obligate (100%) finding across all KDM2B pathogenic variants or whether domain-specific mechanisms (dominant-negative vs. haploinsufficiency) dictate penetrance, explaining reports of incomplete penetrance in pLOF/JmjC variants.

evidence.text: van Oirsouw et al. (2026) report that while CxxC-domain variants exhibit a highly penetrant clinical phenotype, loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants show incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: We observe a highly penetrant CxxC-related phenotype with distinct facial features supported by GestaltMatcher. In contrast, our findings point to variable expressivity and incomplete penetrance of loss-of-function variants and JmjC domain variants complicating variant classification and genetic counseling.

evidence.text: All 19 evaluated individuals harboring KDM2B CxxC domain variants presented with developmental delay (primarily speech and motor) and intellectual disability.

source.title: KDM2B variants in the CxxC domain impair its DNA-binding ability and cause a distinct neurodevelopmental syndrome
source.quote: All individuals with CxxC variants presented with developmental delay, mainly in the speech and motor domain, in addition to variable intellectual disability and mild facial dysmorphism.

hypotheses.text: The frequency of congenital heart defects in KDM2B-related disorder is domain-dependent, exceeding 75% in individuals with CxxC domain variants while occurring in 60% of pLOF variants and dropping below 30% in contiguous 12q24.31 microdeletions.
hypotheses.rationale: Previous literature assumed a homogeneous 50-70% CHD penetrance across OMIM #621474; testing this proposition will confirm whether CxxC variants carry a significantly higher cardiac burden compared to pure haploinsufficiency or microdeletions.

evidence.text: Congenital heart defects were identified in 14/18 individuals with CxxC domain variants, 3/5 with pLOF variants, and 3/12 individuals with 12q24.31 microdeletions.

source.title: Comprehensive Assessment of the KDM2B‐Associated Neurodevelopmental Disorder and the 12q24. 31 Microdeletion Syndrome
source.quote: Congenital heart defects were present in 12q24.31 (3/12) and KDM2B (14/18 CxxC, 3/5 pLOF) cohorts…

evidence.text: Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals carrying KDM2B CxxC domain variants.

source.quote: Congenital heart defects were observed in up to 78% of individuals, with additional common findings including musculoskeletal, ophthalmological, and urogenital anomalies, as well as behavioral challenges and feeding difficulties.

hypotheses.text: The reported 100% obligate penetrance of intellectual disability in initial discovery cohorts of OMIM #621474 is an artifact of ascertainment bias toward pediatric probands referred for unexplained syndromic developmental delay.
hypotheses.rationale: Initial cohorts ascertained individuals based on clinical presentations of NDD, artificially inflating penetrance estimates to 100%, which becomes challenged as familial testing and broader cohort analyses identify mildly affected or non-penetrant carriers of truncating or JmjC variants.

evidence.text: Initial cohorts recruited individuals specifically presenting with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability to establish the syndrome and define episignatures.

source.title: Delineation of a KDM2B-related neurodevelopmental disorder and its associated DNA methylation signature
source.quote: Individuals in this cohort present with developmental delay and/or intellectual disability; autism; attention deficit disorder/attention deficit hyperactivity disorder; congenital organ anomalies mainly of the heart, eyes, and urogenital system; and subtle facial dysmorphism.

evidence.text: Comprehensive follow-up assessment of expanded cohorts (n=68) demonstrated that loss-of-function and JmjC domain variants display incomplete penetrance and variable expressivity.

new_directions.question_text: What specific congenital heart defect subtypes (e.g., ASD, VSD, tetralogy of Fallot, or valve malformations) distinguish KDM2B CxxC-domain variants from 12q24.31 microdeletions and other chromatin-associated NDDs?
new_directions.rationale: Identifying specific lesion patterns will refine bedside differentiation and clarify whether CxxC variants drive distinct cardiac morphogenetic defects compared to broad chromosomal haploinsufficiency.

new_directions.question_text: What proportion of asymptomatic or mildly affected parents transmit pathogenic KDM2B pLOF or JmjC variants, and what modifier mechanisms account for the incomplete penetrance?
new_directions.rationale: Clarifying familial inheritance rates and incomplete penetrance is essential for accurate genetic counseling and variant reclassification under ACMG/AMP criteria.
